title: unified-capability-endpoint-and-openai-compat-shim
author: Amaya Chen
description:
Motivation: Product teams need a single, queryable surface to discover model capabilities, pricing tiers, and OpenAI-compatibility hints for routing and SDK fallbacks. Current model-listing endpoints scatter hints across several fields and duplicate logic in SDK shims. This PR introduces a unified /v1/models/capabilities endpoint (and corresponding openai-compat shim enhancements) to centralize capability flags (streaming, function_calling, structured_output), pricing/limits info, regional availability, and compatibility metadata.

Summary of changes: - New API: GET /v1/models/capabilities with query filters (capabilities, region, min_qps, openai_compatible=true|false, price_tier). Responses include a standardized capability set and price/limit objects. - Backwards compatibility: existing /v1/models and /v1/models/:id behavior unchanged; clients can opt-in to the new endpoint. The OpenAI-compat layer now consults the capabilities endpoint when resolving model choice for streaming and function-calling fallbacks. - Capability flags expanded: streaming_support (bool), streaming_latency_hint ("low"|"medium"|"best-effort"), function_calling (bool), structured_output_schema (optional JSON-schema URL string), kv_cache_supported (bool). - Pricing and limits: each model listing includes price_per_1k_tokens (float string in USD), max_tokens_supported (int string), recommended_batch_size (int string), and soft_qps_limit (int string). These are advisory and used by Redwood Optimize and routing decisions. - Query filters server-side: filter_by_capabilities (comma-separated), min_price_tier, region, and openai_compatible. Filtering is implemented efficiently using the existing catalog index and a new capability inverted index populated at model onboarding time.

Checklist:
- [x] API contract defined and documented in API spec.
- [x] Server implementation with pagination and filter validation.
- [x] OpenAI-compat shim updates to prefer models that advertise matching capabilities.
- [x] Unit tests for capability parsing, filter combinators, and price/limit format validation.
- [x] Integration tests covering streaming fallback and function-calling route selection.
- [x] Docs and SDK examples updated (Python and TS quickstarts).

Backward compatibility and rollout: This change is additive. Existing clients keep current behavior. The new endpoint is gated behind a feature flag (default on in staging, opt-in in prod for first 48h) and will be rolled to all regions after monitoring. The openai-compat shim will prefer models with matching flags but will fall back to previous selection logic if no capability match is found.

API contract (excerpt): GET /v1/models/capabilities?q=filter_by_capabilities=function_calling,streaming&region=us-west-2&openai_compatible=true&page_size=50
Response shape (fields): id, name, capabilities (csv flags), streaming_support, streaming_latency_hint, function_calling, structured_output_schema, price_per_1k_tokens_usd, max_tokens_supported, recommended_batch_size, soft_qps_limit, regions (list), openai_compatible_hint. All numeric values are returned as strings for stable parsing across SDKs.

Tests and CI: Initial CI run failed lint in api/specs (minor formatting); fixed in second commit. Unit test coverage added for catalog filter combinations and migration logic. Integration tests simulate a streaming-enabled model and validate that the openai shim reroutes requests to streaming-optimized endpoints when streaming_support=true and latency_hint=low.

Documentation and SDKs: API spec markdown added under docs/api/models-capabilities.md. Python and Typescript SDKs get a small helper (get_models_by_capabilities) that calls the new endpoint and normalizes returned fields into sdk-friendly types. Quickstart example demonstrates selecting a model capable of tool/function calling and streaming simultaneously.

Security and cost notes: Pricing fields are advisory; routing decisions should always respect tenant quotas. No sensitive data added to the catalog. All catalog writes are authenticated via existing model registry ACLs.

Related tickets: ENG-1289 (catalog capability indexing), PM-452 (product requirements for model discoverability), SUP-341 (support request for clearer streaming guarantees).

Rolling to production: staged feature flag, 48h telemetry window focusing on: 1) error rate for the new endpoint, 2) percent of requests using capability-driven routing, 3) latency P95 for streaming-handshake when routed via shim.

If merged: release notes will mention the new endpoint and the SDK helper. Migration: customers using custom model-selection logic should evaluate adopting the endpoint to simplify routing and to get advisory pricing/limits in a single call.

review_comments: Diego Marquez: Can we ensure the streaming_latency_hint semantics are documented somewhere central? I want clear guidance for SDKs (low/medium/best-effort).
Amaya Chen: Added a section in docs/api/models-capabilities.md describing semantics and recommended client behavior; SDK helpers normalize the hint into enums.
Priya Nair: Tests look good. One request: validate price_per_1k_tokens format strictly (e.g. two decimals).
Amaya Chen: Tightened validation and added unit test for price format; server returns string but validation enforces decimal format with up to 4 places for future micro-pricing.
Samir Patel: Concern: capability index migration could be slow for customers with very large registries. Can we background this and expose a health indicator?
Amaya Chen: Migration runs as a background job with a shard-friendly cursor; added metrics and a /internal/catalog/migration-status endpoint (auth-protected) to monitor progress.
Diego Marquez: CI initially failed linting on api/specs. Fixed in m3n4o5 commit. Approving post-fix.
Priya Nair: Approve. Verified integration test that simulates function_calling routing and structured_output_schema handling.
Samir Patel: Approve after migration-run telemetry added.
release_notes: Add new GET /v1/models/capabilities endpoint to expose centralized model capability flags, pricing hints, and regional availability; SDK helpers in Python and TS added. Backwards compatible and gated behind feature flag during rollout.
notes: Feature flagged rollout: opt-in in prod for 48h, then enable by default if telemetry looks normal.
No breaking changes to existing /v1/models endpoints.
Telemetry dashboards added: Catalog > Capabilities Usage, Routing > OpenAI-compat selection.
Follow-up work: add UI filters in Console (ENG-1402), and add cost-aware routing examples in Redwood Optimize (PM-470).
